The Iran conflict is becoming a military and economic quagmire, while also unfolding into a political nightmare for the Republicans, who are trailing the Democrats by around 8.5 points ahead of the midterm elections. Now, the prospect of Republicans losing not only the House but also the Senate appears increasingly likely. Should that happen, President Trump will not only spend his last two years in office as a lame duck, but also face impeachment for the third time. If he loses the Senate, he might even be convicted. The President built a reputation as a tough boss who holds associates accountable when things go wrong and doesn’t hesitate to fire people when necessary. It’s high time he examines the detrimental role played by his friend and de facto ‘regional governor’ of the Middle East, Tom Barrack. The disastrous advice and dangerous maneuvers of the U.S. Ambassador to Turkey are largely responsible for present developments, which threaten to cost Republicans the Congress.

The “NO” uttered by dictator Ioannis Metaxas to Mussolini makes—and will continue to make—Greeks feel proud. PARIS (AP) — Police arrested at least 1,800 people across France after violent groups clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations that drew hundreds of thousands of people who denounced rising living costs and poor conditions in schools. Authorities said masked groups on Saturday set fires and attacked public buildings, including city halls, in several cities. In Limoges, a city in central France, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall, causing its roof to collapse. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate told LCI television that the fire was deliberately set and nearly destroyed the building. The fire was under control Sunday.
